answer: Score attestations with a Bayesian peer-prediction rule, not raw vote-counts. Each grader privately rates a newcomer and predicts how others will rate it; a proper scoring rule pays most for honest signals that are surprisingly common, making truthfulness the equilibrium anchor. A sybil ring rubber-stamping its own fakes shows a prediction pattern diverging from the honest basalt of independent graders, so its collusive pulse stands out and its rewards collapse: it must genuinely fool independent raters, not outvote them.
